Subject: High p99 & errors this morning — token backlog / cache churn

Michael / Laura,

We're seeing a significant spike in p99 inference latency and a rising error rate starting ~07:40 PDT. Throughput appears capped — our throughput graphs show a sustained backlog of in-flight requests and many 429/503 errors. Attachments: perf_dump.tar.gz with sampler traces and the liveliness metrics.

Observations from our side:
- p50 stable, p95 up ~30%, p99 up 4-5x
- Error rate (5xx) jumped from 0.2% to ~3% in the last 45m
- KV cache hit rate has dropped ~18% coincident with a spike in prefetch activity on the model serving lanes
- When we correlate traces we see long waits on the primary batch lane — looks like head-of-line blocking while other lanes get prefetched content evicted quickly (cache churn)

This is impacting customers on route /api/v1/generate and one of our most critical flows is timing out. Can you triage? We need immediate mitigation plus an ETA for a longer fix.

Thanks,
Sofia Alvarez
Platform Engineering, Acme Robotics

Subject: Re: High p99 & errors this morning — token backlog / cache churn

Thanks — dug into the traces. Quick notes:
- Confirmed: prefetch queue for the hot model (gptx-13b-v2) spiked; the prefetching workers are allocating KV slots aggressively which causes eviction of recently used prefixes belonging to active requests.
- Observed a short window where batch lanes are waiting on a single inflight request for >800ms while other lanes are blocked on the same cold prefix (classic HOL).

Suggested immediate steps (apply to affected pool only):
1) set service.runtime.max_prefetch: 0.25
2) service.runtime.conservative_kv_eviction: true
3) increase batch_lane_count by +1 to add parallelism for short sequences
4) temporarily disable aggressive prefix-prefetch for requests with seq_len < 64

I've prepared a candidate kv_config.yaml (attached). We should patch the pool and route ~10% of traffic to the patched pool as a canary before full roll. If canary shows >50% reduction in p99 we expand.

Command to flip (run in infra admin):
- redwoodctl pool patch --pool-id pool-acme-1 --file kv_config.yaml
- redwoodctl route update --route /api/v1/generate --pool pool-acme-1-canary --weight 10

Attachment: kv_config.yaml (candidate)

Markus
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec update: Acme Robotics prefetch-induced HOL stalls — mitigation & next steps

Laura / Marissa — brief executive summary for your visibility and any required approvals:

Incident: 07:40 PDT — Acme Robotics reported increased p99 latency and a spike in 5xx errors affecting /api/v1/generate. Root cause (initial): aggressive prefix prefetching causing KV slot churn and head-of-line blocking on hot prefixes.

Impact: Acme production tenants experienced degraded latency (p99 up 4–5x) and transient 429/503 errors. Customer reports some timeouts on robotic control pipelines — high business impact for this account (strategic).

Action taken:
- Canaried a config patch to pool-acme-1 at 09:15 PDT with reduced prefetch and conservative eviction.
- Initial canary (10% traffic) dropped p99 by ~60% and reduced 5xx rate to baseline within 25 minutes.
- Ramped to 100% over 45 minutes with monitoring.

Request: Approve a formal maintenance window (2–4 hours) to apply the config change cluster-wide for other similar pools and to run a short reindexing of KV metrics to avoid recurrence. Also requesting approval for a one-time service credit for Acme (proposal: 7% of last month invoice) to cover business impact and preserve relationship.

Mitigation plan (next 48h):
- Code change to limit prefetch aggressiveness based on per-tenant sequence histograms. (Engineering: Markus)
- Add a short-term admission control to ensure single-request HOL time < 250ms per lane.
- Postmortem to include improved alerting thresholds for early prefetch/backlog signals.

Happy to discuss live.

—Michael
Head of Customer Engineering
